intro: Interview patterns repeat hote hain: two pointers, sliding window, prefix sums, stack, hashing aur interval merge. Is section me har pattern ka ek chhota, runnable example hai — inhe pehchan kar naye problem me apply karna hi asli practice hai.
theory: Two pointers tab lagta hai jab sorted array me pair/range dhoondhna ho; dono ends se move karke O(n) milta hai.
Sliding window contiguous subarray/substring problems ke liye hai: window grow karo, condition fail hone par shrink karo.
Prefix sums range-sum queries ko O(1) me badalte hain, kyunki sum(l..r) = prefix[r+1] - prefix[l].
Stack matching brackets aur nested structure ke liye natural hai; LIFO order validation ko simple banata hai.
Grouping problems me canonical key (sorted string, tuple) banao aur hash map me group karo — O(n) average.

prefix = [0]
for value in nums:

range_sum = prefix[r + 1] - prefix[l]

Output ko print se verify karo.

Sieve multiples ko mark karke primes O(n log log n) me nikalta hai.

Interval merge calendar/booking systems me overlapping slots combine karne ke liye use hota hai.

interview.q: Sliding window kab apply karte hain?
interview.a: Jab contiguous subarray/substring par condition monotonic ho — window grow karne par constraint bigadta hai aur shrink karne par sudharta hai. Negative numbers ke saath sum-window aksar nahi chalta.

interview.q: Prefix sum ka trade-off kya hai?
interview.a: O(n) preprocessing se range sum O(1), par array update ho to prefix rebuild O(n) lagta hai. Static data ke liye perfect; dynamic ke liye Fenwick/segment tree.

interview.q: Stack se bracket validation kyun kaam karta hai?
interview.a: Brackets nested hote hain aur last opened sabse pehle close hota hai — LIFO exactly wahi order hai. End me stack empty hona chahiye.

interview.q: Anagram grouping ki complexity kya hai?
interview.a: Har word ko sort karke key banane me O(k log k), total O(n·k log k). Counting key se O(n·k) possible hai par alphabet size ke hisaab se.

coding.question: Coding lab 2: implement sliding_window and print the result.
coding.build: Fixed-size window ko slide karke sum O(1) me update hota hai. Ek chhota runnable example likho jo output print kare.
coding.input: sliding_window ke liye sample data snippet me diya hai
coding.expected: Printed output sliding_window ka result dikhata hai
coding.hint: Solution ka core sliding_window hai; output ko readable rakho.
coding.concept: Coding Patterns, Projects & Final Practice · sliding_window
coding.solution:
nums = [2, 1, 5, 1, 3, 2]
k = 3
best = sum(nums[:k])
current = best
for i in range(k, len(nums)):
    current += nums[i] - nums[i - k]
    best = max(best, current)
print(best)
coding.explanation: Fixed-size window ko slide karke sum O(1) me update hota hai. Isliye example seedha result print karta hai, taaki behaviour verify ho sake.

debugging.why: String concatenation ko dono taraf str chahiye; Python implicit conversion nahi karta. Ye Coding Patterns, Projects & Final Practice ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: f-string ya str() se explicit conversion karo.
debugging.lesson: TypeError type mismatch batata hai — conversion explicit karo.

debugging.error: IndexError: list index out of range
debugging.why: List me sirf 0 aur 1 index hain; 5 par kuch nahi. Ye Coding Patterns, Projects & Final Practice ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: Index se pehle length check karo ya safe getter use karo.
debugging.correct:

print(scores[1] if len(scores) > 1 else None)
debugging.lesson: IndexError off-by-one aur empty collection ka signal hai.

debugging.why: Dict me score key exist nahi karti; [] missing key par KeyError deta hai. Ye Coding Patterns, Projects & Final Practice ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: get() se default do ya key ki presence check karo.
debugging.lesson: KeyError expected-missing field ka case hai — get/default se handle karo.

debugging.error: ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '12.5'

debugging.fix: Pehle float() phir int() karo, ya Decimal use karo.
debugging.lesson: ValueError format ka issue hai, type ka nahi.

projects.objective: two_pointers aur sliding_window ka demo jo output print kare.
projects.code:
nums = [1, 2, 4, 7, 11]
target = 9
left, right = 0, len(nums) - 1
while left < right:
    total = nums[left] + nums[right]
    if total == target:
        print(nums[left], nums[right])
        break
    if total < target:
        left += 1
    else:
        right -= 1
nums = [2, 1, 5, 1, 3, 2]
k = 3
best = sum(nums[:k])
current = best
for i in range(k, len(nums)):
    current += nums[i] - nums[i - k]
    best = max(best, current)
print(best)
projects.explanation: Sorted array par two pointers pair ko linear time me dhoondhte hain. Fixed-size window ko slide karke sum O(1) me update hota hai. Dono snippets ek hi file me chalte hain.
